name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: Copies sixteen 32-bit values from a fixed offset in the base block into the buffer whose pointer is passed on the stack, skipping the copy when that pointer is null. It then calls the code address held in a second register and returns.

name: wrap_call_with_conditional_setup
description: Clears a flag byte, looks up a task-related structure through a dispatch table, and if a status field in it is zero runs a setup routine and stores its result in the flag. It then calls the wrapped routine and, when the flag is set, runs a teardown pair before returning that routine's result.

name: initialize_and_run_service_loop
description: Sets up a group of global counters and hardware-register pointers, calls a series of setup routines, then loops indefinitely. Each pass advances a counter pair, polls an input-related table, and either waits and returns or runs a block of routines that update the same counters.

name: allocate_free_slot_record
description: Checks whether the table byte at the given index is free; if it is and the running offset is below 248, it marks the slot with its index, writes a four-byte record at the current offset and advances the offset by four. It returns the stored index or the unchanged offset.

name: append_slot_record_if_room
description: Writes a slot index byte and a two-word record at the current offset when the offset is below 248, then advances the offset by four. Nothing is written when the offset has reached the limit.

name: store_slot_record_and_advance
description: Writes a slot index byte and a two-word record at the current position unconditionally, then advances the position counter stored at the given address by four.

name: partition_entries_into_buckets
description: Clears a block of counters, copies sixteen-bit keys from a list and then repeatedly partitions a range of 32-bit entries by a nibble-derived key using a stack of sub-ranges. Each finished range is stored as an offset and count into a lookup table, with two helper routines called around the partition steps.

name: compute_component_extrema_and_spans
description: Initialises six min/max slots to extreme values, then scans a run of 32-bit words splitting each into an 8-bit field and two 4-bit fields. It tracks the minimum and maximum of each field and stores the three individual spans and their total.

name: clear_shifted_mask_across_bitplanes
description: Clears pixels in eight screen rows across four bitplanes using a mask table read with a fixed row stride, shifted by the horizontal offset held in the low nibble of the argument. When the shift takes the mask into the adjacent column, the neighbouring pixels are cleared as well.

name: clear_mask_rows_from_registers
description: Clears pixels in eight screen rows across four bitplanes using a byte mask shifted by a horizontal offset passed in a register. It uses the same clearing logic as its sibling for the shifted case but takes its table and screen pointers from registers.

name: clear_bit_column_rows
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and clearing the resulting pixels in all four bitplanes of one screen column, advancing one 40-byte row per byte. The routine has no return value and touches only the screen buffer.

name: write_colour_one_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index one: the shifted mask is ORed into the first bitplane and cleared from the other three. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, and a second path handles the case where the shift spills into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_one_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index one, setting the bits in the first bitplane and clearing them in the other three. It takes its source table and screen pointer from registers and uses the same clearing logic as its table-driven sibling.

name: write_colour_one_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first bitplane while clearing them in the other three, one 40-byte row per byte. It writes only screen memory.

name: write_colour_two_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index two: the shifted mask is set in the second bitplane and cleared from the first, third and fourth. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_two_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index two, setting the bits in the second bitplane and clearing them in the others. Table and screen pointers come from registers, and the routine has no return value.

name: write_colour_two_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the second bitplane while clearing them in the first, third and fourth, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_three_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index three: the shifted mask is set in the first and second bitplanes and cleared from the other two. It uses a mask table with a fixed row stride and a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_three_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index three, setting the bits in the first and second bitplanes and clearing them in the other two. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_three_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first and second bitplanes while clearing them in the third and fourth, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_four_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index four: the shifted mask is set in the third bitplane and cleared from the other three. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_four_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index four, setting the bits in the third bitplane and clearing them in the others. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_four_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the third bitplane while clearing them in the other three, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_five_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index five: the shifted mask is set in the first and third bitplanes and cleared from the second and fourth. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_five_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index five, setting the bits in the first and third bitplanes and clearing them in the second and fourth. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_five_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first and third bitplanes while clearing them in the second and fourth, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_six_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index six: the shifted mask is set in the second and third bitplanes and cleared from the first and fourth. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_six_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index six, setting the bits in the second and third bitplanes and clearing them in the first and fourth. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_six_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the second and third bitplanes while clearing them in the first and fourth, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_seven_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index seven: the shifted mask is set in the first, second and third bitplanes and cleared from the fourth. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_seven_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index seven, setting the bits in the first three bitplanes and clearing them in the fourth. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_seven_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first three bitplanes while clearing them in the fourth, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_eight_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index eight: the shifted mask is set in the fourth bitplane and cleared from the first three. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_eight_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index eight, setting the bits in the fourth bitplane and clearing them in the first three. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_eight_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the fourth bitplane while clearing them in the first, second and third bitplanes, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_nine_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 9: the shifted mask is set in the first and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the second and third bitplanes. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_nine_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 9, setting the bits in the first and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the second and third bitplanes. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_nine_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the second and third bitplanes, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_ten_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 10: the shifted mask is set in the second and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the first and third bitplanes. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_ten_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 10, setting the bits in the second and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the first and third bitplanes. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_ten_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the second and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the first and third bitplanes, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_eleven_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 11: the shifted mask is set in the first, second and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the third bitplane. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_eleven_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 11, setting the bits in the first, second and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the third bitplane. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_eleven_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first, second and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the third bitplane, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_twelve_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 12: the shifted mask is set in the third and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the first and second bitplanes. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_twelve_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 12, setting the bits in the third and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the first and second bitplanes. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_twelve_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the third and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the first and second bitplanes, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_thirteen_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 13: the shifted mask is set in the first, third and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the second bitplane. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_thirteen_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 13, setting the bits in the first, third and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the second bitplane. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_thirteen_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first, third and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the second bitplane, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_fourteen_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 14: the shifted mask is set in the second, third and fourth bitplanes and cleared from the first bitplane. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_fourteen_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 14, setting the bits in the second, third and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in the first bitplane. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_fourteen_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the second, third and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in the first bitplane, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: write_colour_fifteen_shifted_mask
description: Writes pixels in eight screen rows for colour index 15: the shifted mask is set in the first, second, third and fourth bitplanes and cleared from none. A mask table with a fixed row stride supplies the bytes, with a spill path into the neighbouring column.

name: write_colour_fifteen_mask_regs
description: Writes eight rows of a shifted mask for colour index 15, setting the bits in the first, second, third and fourth bitplanes and clearing them in none. Table and screen pointers come from registers.

name: write_colour_fifteen_bit_column
description: Walks a byte array, shifting each byte by a bit offset and setting the resulting pixels in the first, second, third and fourth bitplanes while clearing them in none, one 40-byte row per byte.

name: wait_then_initialise_control_block
description: Waits until a status word at a fixed offset from the base block reads zero, then writes a control byte, a constant word and a long pointer taken from a global, and sets several adjacent words to fixed values including a negative marker.

name: initialise_control_block
description: Writes a negative marker, a long pointer taken from a global, and several constant words into fixed offsets of the base block without waiting for any status. It returns immediately afterwards.

name: call_then_wait_status_clear
description: Calls a routine and then waits in a loop until a status word at a fixed offset from the base block reads zero, before returning.

name: wait_write_command_and_wait
description: Waits for a status word to read zero, writes a constant word and a zero byte into the block, calls a helper routine, and waits for the status word to clear again before returning.

name: wait_write_alt_command_wait
description: Waits for a status word to read zero, writes a different constant word and a zero byte into the block, calls a helper routine, and waits for the status word to clear again before returning.

name: call_routine_from_base_slot
description: Calls the code address stored in the first long word at the base pointer it is given, then returns.

name: run_four_routines_in_sequence
description: Calls four helper routines one after another with no other work, then returns.

name: setup_and_parse_text_script
description: Stores a pointer from a global table, indexed by the argument, and a position word into the state block, then walks a byte-coded text script. Printable bytes go to a glyph helper while the horizontal position is below a limit, control bytes change the position or select another pointer, and a zero byte ends the walk.

name: init_and_parse_text_script
description: Reads a width byte and a vertical byte from the script, stores a glyph helper address and the doubled width in the state block, then walks the byte-coded text script. Control codes adjust the position or select a pointer, and printable bytes are drawn while the horizontal position is below a limit.

name: parse_text_script_from_position
description: Walks a byte-coded text script from the current state, passing printable bytes to a glyph helper while the horizontal position is below a limit. Control codes move the position, select a pointer from a global table, or advance a vertical position by ten until it passes a limit.

name: run_text_script_state_machine
description: Walks a byte-coded text script through a state loop that reads control codes, moves the horizontal and vertical position, and passes printable bytes to a glyph helper below a horizontal limit. It stops at a zero byte or when the vertical position passes its limit.

name: resume_text_script_parsing
description: Continues walking a byte-coded text script from a reentry point, emitting printable bytes through a glyph helper below a horizontal limit and handling control codes for position, pointer selection and vertical advance.

name: parse_text_script_from_control
description: Walks a byte-coded text script from a control-code entry point, passing printable bytes to a glyph helper while the horizontal position is below a limit. Control codes move the position, select a pointer from a global table, or advance a vertical position by ten until it passes a limit.

name: advance_row_then_parse_script
description: Advances the vertical position of a text script by ten and stops when it passes a limit, otherwise restarts the byte walk from the saved row. Printable bytes go to a glyph helper below a horizontal limit, and control codes select pointers or change the position.

name: set_text_entry_skip_string
description: If the vertical position is below a limit, stores a pointer from a global table and a position word into the state block, then advances the text pointer past its zero-terminated string.

name: skip_text_control_to_end
description: Walks a zero-terminated text stream, skipping the operand bytes of each control code. One control code stores a pointer from a global table into the state block, and the walk stops at the terminating zero.

name: scan_to_zero_terminator
description: Advances the text pointer one byte at a time until it reaches a zero byte, then returns with the pointer on that terminator.

name: scan_text_control_to_end
description: Walks a zero-terminated text stream, storing a pointer from a global table when a particular control code appears, and stops at the terminating zero byte.

name: scan_string_to_terminator
description: Advances the text pointer past a zero-terminated string and leaves it on the terminating zero byte.

name: walk_triangle_scanlines
description: Sorts three points by their vertical coordinate, computes fixed-point slopes for the edges, and steps down the scanlines. For each row with a valid width it calls a span routine through a jump table, and it stops once the row count is exhausted.

name: walk_stack_argument_edge_pair
description: Computes fixed-point edge steps from the coordinates in the stack argument and the register pair, walks the scanlines of the first edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with valid width, then does the same for the second edge.

name: walk_edge_pair_second_setup
description: Sets up fixed-point edge steps from the stack arguments and register values, walks the first edge's rows through a span routine table, then derives a second edge from the same points and walks its rows the same way.

name: walk_single_fixed_slope_edge
description: Walks the rows of one fixed-point edge whose step comes from the stack arguments, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width, then walks the remaining rows of the other edge.

name: walk_two_edge_scanlines_regs
description: Walks scanlines along two fixed-point edges, one derived from register values and one from the stack arguments, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: finish_edge_scanlines_setup_second
description: Walks the rows of an edge already set up in registers, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row, then computes the other edge from the stack arguments and walks its rows.

name: walk_single_edge_scanlines
description: Walks scanlines along one fixed-point edge derived from register values, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: walk_offset_edge_scanlines
description: Computes a fixed-point edge step from register values and walks its rows from an offset-adjusted start, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: walk_one_edge_span_loop
description: Walks a block of rows along one fixed-point edge, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: sort_vertices_walk_edges
description: Repeatedly selects the vertex with the smallest vertical coordinate from three by comparing them, computes fixed-point edge steps from the sorted points, and walks the scanlines, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: walk_register_edge_pair_scanlines
description: Computes fixed-point edge steps for two edges from register values and walks their scanlines, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: forward_stack_args_to_walker
description: Passes its two stack arguments on to a scanline walker routine and returns, adding no work of its own.

name: walk_stack_edge_pair_scanlines
description: Computes fixed-point edge steps from the stack arguments and register values, then walks the scanlines of two edges, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: setup_and_forward_scanline_args
description: Sets up a few register values from its arguments, then passes them to a scanline walker routine before returning.

name: walk_stack_argument_scanline_pair
description: Sets up fixed-point edge steps from the stack arguments and walks the scanlines of two edges, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row with a valid width.

name: walk_stack_edge_scanlines_clip
description: Walks scanlines along two fixed-point edges whose start values come from the stack arguments, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row whose horizontal extent lies within the screen width. It then returns.

name: walk_edge_scanlines_if_tall
description: Walks the rows of two fixed-point edges only when the vertical extent is at least the row count held in a register, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_pair_if_tall
description: Checks that the vertical span is at least the row count from its arguments, then walks two fixed-point edges row by row, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_rows_then_step_stack
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, then computes a step from the stack argument pair for the following edge.

name: walk_register_edge_scanlines_short
description: Walks the rows of two fixed-point edges set up from register values, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_single_edge_rows_offset
description: Walks the rows of one fixed-point edge from an offset starting value, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_scanline_rows_counted
description: Walks a block of rows along a fixed-point edge, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, and stops when its row counter reaches the sentinel value.

name: walk_edge_rows_stack_step
description: Derives a fixed-point step from the stack argument pair and register values, walks the rows of the edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, then updates the second argument pair.

name: walk_edge_rows_update_stack
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, then computes a divided step and writes it back into the second argument pair.

name: walk_edge_rows_registers
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge set up entirely from register values, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_wide_start
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge from a wide starting value, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_scanline_rows_countdown
description: Counts down a row total while walking a fixed-point edge, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_split_edge_stack_pair
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge that is split at a midpoint, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width. The stack argument pair supplies the start values of the second part.

name: walk_split_edge_stack_setup
description: Sets up fixed-point steps for the two halves of a split edge from the stack arguments, then walks each half row by row, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_if_wide
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge only when the horizontal distance from the arguments is at least the width in a register, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_conditional_pair
description: Walks the rows of two fixed-point edges when the horizontal distance meets a threshold, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_divide_stack
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, then divides the stack argument pair to derive the next edge step.

name: walk_edge_rows_register_pair
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge whose start and step come from a register pair, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_wide_regs
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge set up from wide register values, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_countdown_plain
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge, counting down the row total and calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_stack_fraction
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge whose fractional step is taken from the stack argument pair, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_then_fraction
description: Computes a fractional step from the stack argument pair, walks the rows of the edge calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, and then sets up the following edge.

name: walk_edge_rows_if_ordered
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge only when its start point is ordered before its end, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_wide_compare
description: Compares two wide values to choose the edge direction, then walks its rows calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width.

name: walk_edge_rows_sentinel_stop
description: Walks the rows of a fixed-point edge, calling a span routine through a jump table for each row within screen width, and stops when the row counter reaches its sentinel value.

name: dispatch_sprite_parts_by_count
description: Returns at once unless the position lies inside the inner area from 2 to 317 across and 2 to 165 down. Otherwise it calls one to four drawing routines taken from pointers in the data block, chosen by the count argument.

name: call_two_table_entries_sequence
description: Calls two code pointers from the data block, each located through a word offset stored in the block, then returns.

name: call_three_table_entries_first
description: Calls three code pointers from the data block, each looked up through a word offset stored in the block, then returns.

name: call_three_table_entries_second
description: Calls three code pointers from the data block through a fixed word offset in each entry, then returns.

name: call_four_table_entries_sequence
description: Calls four code pointers from the data block in sequence, each located through a word offset stored in the block, then returns.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: dispatch_bounded_parts_by_count
description: Returns unless the position lies inside the area from 2 to 317 across and 2 to 165 down. Otherwise it runs a different sequence of pointer calls from the data block for each count value, from one call up to several parts.

name: build_edge_word_table_pairs
description: Fills paired word tables for left and right edges by stepping position values for each scanline, writing a computed word into both tables as it advances through the rows.

name: clip_pair_list_call_span
description: Walks a list of word pairs, clipping each horizontal run to the 320-pixel screen width and calling a span routine through a jump table for each visible run, for a row count derived from the arguments.

name: fill_edge_table_while_stepping
description: Steps left and right edge values row by row while building their word table entries, continuing until the edge positions cross the row limit.

name: walk_record_list_clipped_draw
description: Loads a record pointer from the global block and walks a list of 16-bit records, clipping each against the horizontal range and calling a drawing routine through a table offset for each record that remains. It stops at a zero record.

name: walk_record_list_part_calls
description: Walks a list of 16-bit records from the global block, testing each record's vertical and horizontal extent and calling several part routines through table offsets for records that fall in range.

name: draw_remaining_records_loop
description: Loops over the remaining records, calling a drawing routine through a table offset for each one and finishing with one last call before returning.

name: walk_sprite_rows_table_calls
description: Calls a row handler found through the data block for each row, repeating until a handler returns the sentinel value. If the starting count is negative it returns the count minus one without any calls.

name: walk_sprite_rows_with_bounds
description: Checks the start and end row counts against each other, then calls a row handler from the data block for each row in range until the handler returns the sentinel value.

name: call_row_handlers_until_sentinel
description: Calls a row handler from a table for each row in turn, skipping the work when the row counter is already zero, and stops once the handler reports the sentinel value.

name: walk_rows_table_calls_countdown
description: Calls a row handler found through the data block for each row, counting down the row total and returning the count minus one when no rows remain.

name: walk_rows_offset_table_calls
description: Calls row handlers from a table selected by a computed offset, looping over the rows until the handler's sentinel result or the row counter ends the walk.

name: call_row_handlers_countdown
description: Calls a row handler from a table for each row, counting down until the row total is exhausted or the handler reports the sentinel value.

name: walk_rows_table_calls_sentinel
description: Calls a row handler from the data block for each row and repeats until the handler returns the sentinel value, with the same zero-count guard as its siblings.

name: walk_rows_bounds_calls_wide
description: Checks start and end row counters against each other and against the sign of a column value, then calls row handlers from a table for each row in the resulting range.

name: call_row_handlers_nested_sentinel
description: Calls a row handler from a table for each row, skipping the work when the row counter is already zero, and stops once the handler reports the sentinel value.

name: walk_rows_table_zero_guard
description: Returns the count minus one at once when it is negative. Otherwise it calls a row handler from the data block for each row until the handler returns the sentinel value.

name: walk_line_points_in_bounds
description: Steps two coordinate pairs held on the stack along a line, calling a point routine for each position inside the 320 by 168 screen area for a count held on the stack. It returns once the count goes negative.

name: clip_line_walk_points
description: Steps a point along a line with fixed-point increments, calling a helper for each point inside the 320 by 168 screen area, and stops once a point leaves that area or the step count runs out.

name: step_line_points_with_count
description: Walks points along a line for a step count taken from the arguments, calling a helper for each position with valid coordinates and returning when the count is exhausted.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: call_four_helpers_then_return
description: Calls four helper routines in sequence and then returns, with no other work.

name: blit_shifted_sprite_rows_clipped
description: Returns if the sprite rectangle lies outside the 320 by 168 screen area. Otherwise it copies the sprite rows into the bitplanes, applying a bit shift when the horizontal offset is not word-aligned.

name: blit_sprite_rows_bounded_200
description: Returns when the sprite lies outside a 320 by 200 area. Otherwise it copies the sprite's rows into the bitplanes, applying a bit shift for horizontal offsets that are not word-aligned.

name: copy_words_into_strided_buffer
description: Copies a run of 16-bit words into a buffer with a fixed ten-byte stride, then repeats the copy for a second plane located 8000 bytes further on.

name: call_table_routine_per_row
description: Looks up a routine pointer from a table indexed by the argument and calls it once per row in a counted loop, then repeats the calls for the remaining rows. The index value 18 is treated as a no-op case.

name: call_table_routine_plain
description: Looks up a routine pointer from a table indexed by the argument and calls it once for each row in a counted loop, then repeats the calls for the following rows before returning.

name: copy_long_word_pair
description: Copies two 16-bit words from one buffer to another, with the second word read from the next position, then returns.

name: copy_two_words
description: Copies two 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_five_words
description: Copies five consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_three_words
description: Copies three consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_seven_words
description: Copies seven consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_four_words
description: Copies four consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_nine_words
description: Copies nine consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_five_words_alt
description: Copies five consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another with the same sequence as its sibling copy routines, then returns.

name: copy_block_with_trailing_value
description: Copies four consecutive entries and then one trailing 16-bit value from one buffer to another, then returns.

name: copy_six_words
description: Copies six consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_six_words_alt
description: Copies six consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another in the same way as its sibling routine, then returns.

name: copy_seven_words_alt
description: Copies seven consecutive 16-bit words from one buffer to another, using a second register copy of the source address, then returns.

name: copy_seven_words_block
description: Copies seven consecutive words from one buffer to another in a straight run, then returns.

name: copy_eight_words
description: Copies eight consecutive words from one buffer to another and returns.

name: copy_eight_words_alt
description: Copies eight consecutive words from one buffer to another with the same sequence as its sibling, then returns.

name: copy_nine_words_alt
description: Copies nine consecutive words from one buffer to another with the same sequence as its sibling copy routines, then returns.

name: copy_nine_words_block
description: Copies nine consecutive words from one buffer to another in a straight run, then returns.

name: merge_shifted_column_into_plane
description: Sets up a row pointer and a mask from the arguments and calls two helper routines. It then merges shifted byte data into a bitplane buffer for each row, keeping the existing bits outside the mask.

name: merge_shifted_values_into_rows
description: Walks a list of byte values, shifting each by a bit offset and merging it into the screen word for each row with a mask that keeps the other bits. The screen pointer advances to the next row after each value.

name: run_four_helper_calls_again
description: Calls four helper routines in sequence and then returns, with no other work.

name: merge_shifted_bytes_plane_rows
description: Merges a run of shifted byte values into screen words row by row, OR-ing each shifted value into the buffer while keeping the other bits, then moves to the next row.

name: return_without_action
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: return_without_action_alt
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: multiply_value_by_thirty_two
description: Returns the 16-bit argument multiplied by 32, done by shifting it left five bits.

name: xor_into_indexed_table_entry
description: XORs a 16-bit value into a table entry chosen by a doubled index from a fixed base address in the data block.

name: fill_clipped_rectangle_rows
description: Handles a rectangle of rows described by a data-block pointer. A negative count calls two helper routines and returns, otherwise it steps through the rows and columns, clipping against a fixed row limit.

name: call_two_helpers_then_return
description: Calls two helper routines in sequence and then returns, with no other work.

name: draw_rows_if_within_limit
description: Clips the row count so the range fits within 198 rows, calls a helper for alignment when needed, then calls a row routine from a table for each remaining row.

name: call_row_routine_countdown
description: Calls a row routine found through the data block once for each row, counting the row total down to zero before returning.

name: multiply_and_normalise_pair
description: Multiplies two 16-bit values and scales the products, then halves both results together until the first lies within plus or minus 7935. The two reduced values are returned packed into one 32-bit result.

name: normalise_pair_to_range
description: Halves a pair of 16-bit values together until the first lies within plus or minus 7935, then halves the second value alone until it lies in the same range.

name: normalise_value_to_range
description: Halves a 16-bit value repeatedly until it lies within plus or minus 7935, then returns.

name: halve_until_below_limit
description: Halves a 16-bit value repeatedly until it no longer exceeds 7935, then returns.

name: return_without_action_second
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: scale_pair_and_normalise
description: Scales two 16-bit values by a shared factor and halves them until the first lies within plus or minus 7935, returning the packed result.

name: reduce_pair_to_range
description: Halves a pair of 16-bit values together until the first is no larger than 7935, then halves the second on its own until it lies within plus or minus 7935.

name: reduce_signed_value_to_range
description: Halves a signed 16-bit value repeatedly until it lies within plus or minus 7935, handling negative and positive values in separate loops.

name: halve_value_above_limit
description: Halves a 16-bit value repeatedly while it exceeds 7935, then returns.

name: return_without_action_third
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to the caller.

name: reduce_fixed_triple_to_range
description: Shifts three fixed-point values right by two bits per step until the first fits a signed 16-bit range, then computes a combined result from the three values.

name: reduce_fixed_point_triple_clamp
description: Shifts a fixed-point triple right by two bits per step until its first value is in range, then clamps the derived value to the limit of the other pair and returns it.

name: reduce_fixed_point_triple_ordered
description: Checks that the second value lies between the negated third value and the third value, then shifts the triple right until the second value is within the 16-bit range.

name: reduce_fixed_point_triple_scaled
description: Shifts the second value of a fixed-point triple right by two bits per step until it fits a signed 16-bit range, scaling the other two values along with it, then computes the result.

name: reduce_fixed_point_triple_branches
description: Compares the fixed-point triple, shifts it into range in one of several branches, and calls helper routines to finish the calculation.

name: scale_pair_table_entry_range
description: Multiplies two values by a table entry chosen by the index argument, then shifts the products down and halves them until the first lies within range.

name: scale_pair_by_table_entry
description: Multiplies two values by a table entry chosen by the index argument and returns both shifted products packed into one result.

name: scale_pair_indexed_table
description: Shifts a fixed-point triple down by bit steps until its high value is small enough, then multiplies the remaining pair by a table value selected from the shifted index.

name: count_doublings_to_top_bit
description: Calls a helper for its value, then counts how many times the value can be doubled before its top bit is set, returning the masked count.

name: lookup_with_offset_or_floor
description: Returns the constant floor value unless the argument exceeds 63; otherwise it calls itself recursively and adds 160 to the result.

name: return_sentinel_minimum_value
description: Returns the constant 32768, the 16-bit value with only its top bit set, which the callers treat as a sentinel.

name: multiply_absolute_fixed_point_pair
description: Takes the absolute values of two 32-bit fixed-point quantities, multiplies their high words through a helper, and returns the packed 64-bit result.

name: divide_fixed_point_values
description: Divides one fixed-point value by another bit by bit, doubling a running remainder and subtracting the divisor on each of many iterations to build up the quotient.
